question_text: Write z = −√7 + i√21 in the polar form.

mark_split.label: Find the amplitude θ from the quadrant and write r(cos θ + i sin θ)

recall_prompt: Say how you would write a complex number in polar form — what two numbers you need and how the quadrant fixes the angle.
insider_note: tan θ = −√3 fits two angles and a calculator picks the wrong one; (−√7, √21) is in the second quadrant, so θ = π − π/3 = 2π/3. Simplify r = √28 to 2√7 — that is the expected form.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find r
steps.margin_note: First mark. x = −√7, y = √21. The squares are 7 and 21, so r = √28 = 2√7.

recall.must_convey: That x = −√7, y = √21 and the modulus r = √(7 + 21) = 2√7.
accept: x is minus root seven, y is root twenty one, r is root of seven plus twenty one which is two root seven
the modulus is root twenty eight equals two root seven
r equals root x squared plus y squared, that is two root seven
modulus root twenty eight, ante two root seven
seven plus twenty one is twenty eight, root of that is two root seven

steps.why: r is the distance of the point from the origin, always positive; the sign of x plays no part here. It is needed as the multiplier in front of the bracket in the polar form.
common_mistakes: Leaving r as √28 — acceptable, but 2√7 is the expected simplified form.

steps.label: Find θ and write the form
steps.margin_note: Second mark. tan θ = y/x = −√3, but that alone gives two candidate angles. The point (−√7, √21) is in the second quadrant, so θ = π − π/3 = 2π/3.

recall.must_convey: That tan θ = −√3 with the point in the second quadrant gives θ = 2π/3, so the polar form is 2√7(cos 2π/3 + i sin 2π/3).
accept: tan theta is minus root three and the point is in the second quadrant so theta is two pi by three
the polar form is two root seven times cos two pi by three plus i sin two pi by three
second quadrant, theta equals pi minus pi by three equals two pi by three
point second quadrant lo undi kabatti theta two pi by three
amplitude two pi by three and modulus two root seven

steps.why: tan θ = −√3 is true for both −π/3 and 2π/3. Only the quadrant of the point fixes which: a negative x and positive y is the second quadrant, where the amplitude is between π/2 and π. The quadrant line is the mark, not the tan value.
common_mistakes: Writing θ = −π/3 from the calculator without checking the quadrant — that point would be in the fourth quadrant.
Forgetting the r in front of the bracket.
Writing cos 2π/3 − i sin 2π/3, which flips the sign of y.
